chains.trait: Front flippers conceal manipulative hands and blubber lids
links: Shallow epicontinental shelves provide abundant hiding spots
Low tidal range and calm swallow seas reduce need for specialized gills
Qu larval-stage homology preserves manual dexterity
Streamlined torsos reduce drag in dense aquatic medium

skill.effect: The creature slips its hidden hands from beneath its flippers to firmly seize prey or nearby objects. It holds onto aquatic targets strongly.

chains.weakness: Hands are slow to deploy; vulnerable to ambush by fast-swimming flankers.
observe: Flippers flex to reveal human-like fingers briefly
Blubbery lids blink slowly against the shallow sun glare
Swimmers manipulate shells with dexterous digits before slipping hands back

journal.en: They hide their hands like pocket knives; one day, they'll remember why.

plausibility.summary: Concealed hands cost drag—posit only for shallow-shelf benthic foraging (≤30–50 m dives, breath-hold), not pelagic pursuit; blubber lids are fat eyelids reducing glare, not novel optics.
fixes: Concealed hands cost drag—posit only for shallow-shelf benthic foraging (≤30–50 m dives, breath-hold), not pelagic pursuit; blubber lids are fat eyelids reducing glare, not novel optics.

analogues.organism: Pinnipeds (California sea lion, Zalophus californianus) retain mobile digits and grasping in foreflippers; sea otter (Enhydra lutris) manual manipulation.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Aquatic medium transmits low-frequency pulses efficiently
Nocturnal temperature inversions trap sound near surface
Pre-sapient social calling avoids metabolic cost of language centers
Nutrient-poor marine diets force energy budget toward basic locomotion

skill.effect: The creature emits a resonant call that draws a companion from the depths nearby. The summoned ally moves strongly through the water.

chains.weakness: Cannot understand complex commands or tool instructions.
observe: Surface breaks occur in synchronized rhythm

journal.en: They speak the sea’s simple grammar.

plausibility.summary: Drop nocturnal terrestrial temperature-inversion link for underwater calls; use reliable marine low-frequency propagation and chorusing instead; keep calls as contact/motivation-grade, not syntax.
fixes: Drop nocturnal terrestrial temperature-inversion link for underwater calls; use reliable marine low-frequency propagation and chorusing instead; keep calls as contact/motivation-grade, not syntax.

analogues.organism: Harbour seal (Phoca vitulina) and bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops) individually distinctive contact calls without recursive syntax.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Both adapt to low-tide shallow seas; Swimmers preserve internal hands for future manipulation, while Finger Fishers elongate digits into ambulatory fish-hooks.
